componentRoleBoundary.note: The instruction sheet carries no caption, no case number and no party block; the four court-filing components all carry the caption. It opens with "This document is not a court filing. It is the instruction sheet for the petition and the proposed order in this packet. Those documents are filed; these instructions are not, and you do not hand this sheet to the clerk." It is footered on its own scheme, "LegalEase instructions — page 1 of 4" through "page 4 of 4", which does not continue the filing pagination, and no court-filing page is footered at all. It sits last in assembly order on every fixture, so nothing filed follows it. Its own step 5 directs the participant to file the verified petition and the proposed Order for Expungement and names nothing else; step 7 directs the certificate of service to be filed after service. It names itself among "WHAT LEGALEASE CAN PREPARE" as "This filing, service and timing sheet", separately from the four documents "that make up the rest of this packet". The rendered component metadata records isCourtFiling false on it and it is the only component the shared process-guidance engine renders.

structuralChecks.method: Per-page word bounding boxes from pdftotext -bbox over all 54 pages: every word on every page falls within x 72.0-544.2 and y 74.9-757.7 on a 612x792 page, so nothing reaches a margin and nothing is clipped. Adjacent words were tested pairwise per baseline band for negative horizontal gap; none was found. Per-page layout text was read line by line for every page. Per-page ink fraction was measured on every page rendered at 110 dpi: minimum 0.00334 on the certificate-of-service execution page, maximum 0.07928 on the second instruction page, and no page at zero. A four-up contact sheet per packet was rendered and looked at page by page, and the three sparse execution pages were additionally read at full resolution. The last written line of every non-final page was tested for a heading standing alone; none is. Petition allegations run 1..8 on all four fixtures and the instruction steps run 1..9 on all four.
structuralChecks.executionPageNote: Three pages per packet carry only an execution block — the judge's signature rule after the proposed order's ordering paragraphs, the petitioner's block after the verification statement, and the petitioner's block after the certificate. Each carries its own label and its own explanatory sentence, each follows the last line of the section it closes rather than a heading, and none is split across a page break. They are continuation pages, not orphans.

contentChecks.feeStatement: $0 is the only amount printed anywhere in the four packets — eight occurrences, twice per packet, once in the petition's BEFORE YOU FILE section and once under the instruction sheet's FEES heading. Both say the statute sets no fee. Both then say in terms that this is not a waiver: "That is the statute setting no fee, and not a fee that anyone has waived — no waiver procedure is asserted here and none is offered through this packet" on the petition, and "That is the statute setting no fee, not a fee that has been waived for you. There is no fee-waiver application to make on this route and no indigency form to file" on the sheet. Every occurrence of the words waived, waiver and indigency in the four packets is inside one of those two negations. Copying, certification, postage and record-retrieval charges are named as separate charges with separate payees and no amount is stated for any of them.
contentChecks.serviceStatement: The prosecuting attorney is named as the service recipient in the petition, in the certificate of service and on the instruction sheet. Each of those three places also says the Division of Criminal Investigation is not a service recipient on this route. The sheet gives the Division exactly one role — where the participant may request their own criminal history record — and says it is not served with the petition. The transmittal of a certified copy of a granted order to the Division is described as the court's own later step, not as a delivery the participant makes.
contentChecks.absentInstrumentStatement: No summons, praecipe, victim-notice, prosecutor-response or Division-of-Criminal-Investigation instrument is generated in any packet. The instruction sheet states the absence of each one and says none is required on this route under the statewide statutes and published statewide guidance. Casper Municipal Court is named once, on the last instruction page, only to say its packets bind that court alone, are not statewide forms and are not used in this packet — no Casper form is reproduced or referenced as usable.
contentChecks.localPracticeFraming: Clerk mechanics that Wyoming does not publish are consistently sent to the participant's own clerk as that court's practice rather than stated as statewide law. The petition says county clerks, municipal courts and circuit courts may have their own local templates or formatting requirements, that which courts do was not established, and that the packet states no local requirement it cannot support. Instruction step 4 sends cover sheet, copy count, paper versus electronic filing, chambers copy and whether the proposed order goes in with the initial filing to that clerk, saying Wyoming publishes no statewide answer to any of them. HOW TO SUBMIT names no portal and no address. The notarisation question is sent to the filing clerk in both the verification component and the sheet. WHAT LEGALEASE CANNOT DO states that no Wyoming county has been surveyed.
contentChecks.formNumberStatement: The petition states that Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form and no statewide proposed-order template, that there is no Wyoming statewide expungement form number for either document, and that it cites none and invents none. The instruction sheet repeats this under OFFICIAL SOURCES. No form number appears anywhere in the four packets.
contentChecks.note: The only automated literal hits across all 54 pages were the word "true" inside the verification sentence. No unresolved placeholder, no undefined, no NaN, no [object Object], no raw boolean and no internal enum value is printed on any page.

actorBoundaryChecks.note: Every proposed order prints four unmarked ( ) finding boxes, an empty rule above JUDGE OF THE ABOVE-ENTITLED COURT, an empty Dated line and blank record lines, and states that it has been granted by nobody and signed by nobody and that nothing on it reports an act by the Court, the prosecuting attorney, a clerk or the Division. On the no-charges-ever-filed variant the case-number field reads "Case No. ______________" with "To be assigned by the clerk", so no clerk entry is populated. Every certificate of service says to complete and sign it only after service has actually been made, that until then it certifies nothing and it must not be filed as though service had already been made; its recipient, address, method boxes and date of service are all empty. The verification's notary block is empty and is prefaced by the statement that whether the filing court requires an oath was not established and must be asked of that clerk.

crossFixtureChecks.note: All four fixtures name Laramie County Circuit Court and Laramie County and no other court or county, except Natrona County, which appears only inside the Casper Municipal Court disclosure. The prosecuting attorney is referred to by office and never by a fabricated name or address. The three fixtures with a filed case carry the criminal caption STATE OF WYOMING versus a defendant with Case No. CR-2024-0417; wy-1401-no-charges-ever-filed-2 carries the in-the-matter caption with the Petitioner as Petitioner, the line "No criminal case was commenced." and a blank case number to be assigned by the clerk. findings.component: wy_nc_1401-certificate-of-service-4 — Certificate of Service on the Prosecuting Attorney
findings.renderedText: Petitioner, self-represented / Printed name: ______________________________ / Sign and date this by hand, in ink, after service has been made, and file it with the clerk.
findings.defect: The certificate of service's execution page tells the participant to date the document and gives them nowhere to do it. The block renders a signature rule, the label "Petitioner, self-represented", one field — "Printed name: ______________________________" — and then the instruction "Sign and date this by hand, in ink, after service has been made, and file it with the clerk." There is no Date line. Every other execution block in the same packet has one: the petition prints Printed name, Address, Telephone and Date under the identical instruction "Sign and date this by hand, in ink, before you file it"; the verification prints Printed name and Date under "Sign and date this by hand, in ink, at the same time as the petition it verifies"; and the proposed order prints "Dated: ______________________" for the Court. The certificate is the only one of the four that carries the date half of the instruction without the field. The "Date of service: ______" line that does exist is a different field with a different meaning — it is inside THE CERTIFICATE section on the preceding page, is separated from the signature by the whole WHY THE DATE MATTERS section and a page break, and records when service was made rather than when the certificate was signed. A self-represented participant following the instruction literally has to write a date onto a page that provides no rule for it.
findings.origin: src/lib/rcap/packets/jurisdictions/wyoming/custom-pleading.ts, the certificate-of-service template's signatureBlock at lines 886-890, which lists "Printed name: ______________________________" and then the instruction line with no "Date: ______________________________________" entry between them. Compare PETITION_SIGNATURE_BLOCK at lines 666-673 and the verification template's signatureBlock at lines 831-836, which both carry one. Not the shared renderer: the shared custom-pleading engine prints signatureBlock lines verbatim and prints the other two blocks correctly from the same code path. Not fixture data: the block is static template text and renders identically on all four fixtures.
findings.verifierGap: The committed verifier constrains this component in several ways — it asserts the certificate says it is completed only after service, that it certifies nothing until then, that "Date of service: _" is left blank, that no address is printed and that service is never stated as already made — but it makes no assertion about the certificate's execution block, and in particular none that pairs the "Sign and date this" instruction with the presence of a Date field. The three signature blocks are not compared against one another anywhere. The omission is therefore unpinned rather than deliberately asserted, and the verifier passes over it.
findings.expectedTreatment: Two corrections close it and the choice belongs to the correction owner, not to this review. Either add "Date: ______________________________________" to the certificate's signatureBlock so it matches the petition and the verification and the instruction has a field to point at, or, if the design intends the date of service to be the only date the participant writes on this component, change the instruction line so it stops asking for a second one. Whichever is chosen, the verifier should gain an assertion tying a signature block's "and date" instruction to a Date field in the same block, so the guarantee the block prints is the guarantee the verifier tests.
findings.correctionOwnerReason: The defect is in src/lib/rcap/packets/jurisdictions/wyoming/custom-pleading.ts and its verifier gap is in scripts/verify-rcap-wyoming-custom-pleading.mjs. The live plan gives both paths to exactly one owner, rcap-wy-custom-pleading-clean-tracks in the custom_pleading lane, and gives them to no other job. A reissued assignment keeps that job id and that module rather than opening a second job over the same files. It is not a shared-renderer defect and it is not the guidance lane's: the instruction sheet correctly describes the certificate as completed when service is actually made and states nothing about a signature date.
findings.supersedesNote: Either correction changes the bytes of the certificate-of-service component on all four fixtures, and therefore the assembled digests of all four court-filing packets and all four participant packets. data/record-clearing/production-factory/packet-proofs/rcap-wy-custom-pleading-clean-tracks.json and data/record-clearing/production-factory/review-manifests/rcap-wy-custom-pleading-clean-tracks.json are integration-owned and must both be regenerated from the corrected verifier's own output before this family is reviewed again. This review is written against the current bytes and does not survive their replacement.
findings.participantHarmNote: Nothing false is stated, no actor boundary is crossed and no outside party's field is populated. The cost is that the operative service document instructs an act it does not accommodate, on the one component whose date the statute's objection window turns on, which is where a self-represented filer is least able to absorb an ambiguity.
